stories.headline: Canada and U.S. Prepare to Resume Formal Trade Talks After Carney-Trump Call
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and U.S. President Donald Trump held what both characterized as a constructive conversation on bilateral trade relations, signaling that formal negotiations could resume within days. Trump indicated the two countries possess the concept of a new agreement, with items like the Keystone XL pipeline discussed. The renewed discussions arrive as Ottawa prepares its upcoming federal budget amid lingering cross-border economic friction.

stories.headline: Prime Minister Calls Six Federal Byelections in Three Provinces for December 7
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced byelections for December 7 in six ridings across Ontario, Quebec, and Saskatchewan, including Scarborough North and Brantford. The contests provide the governing Liberals an opening to bolster their narrow majority, with former Desjardins head Guy Cormier confirmed as a candidate in Laurier—Sainte-Marie. The votes will also serve as a key test for Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre following recent opposition challenges.

stories.headline: Federal Government to Unveil New Budget as Poilievre Sets Out Fiscal Demands
stories.summary: The federal government will table its next budget this week, featuring targeted affordability relief, business tax incentives, and capital investments in infrastructure and defence. Ahead of the presentation, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre demanded that Ottawa eliminate all federal diesel taxes until Canada Day. The budget will test the governing Liberals' economic management amid ongoing trade instability with the United States.

stories.headline: Federal Liberals Outraise Conservatives by Nearly $1 Million in Third Quarter
stories.summary: Official filings from Elections Canada show the federal Liberal Party collected nearly $1 million more in donations than the Conservatives during the third quarter of 2026. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre criticized the outcome, claiming the governing party leaned on corporate influence supported by public expenditures. The fundraising figures underscore a competitive landscape as both major parties prepare for a slate of winter byelections.

stories.headline: Carney Attends Commonwealth Summit to Diversify Trade and Strengthen International Ties
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has traveled to Antigua and Barbuda to participate in the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, where he will meet King Charles and foreign counterparts. Canadian officials are using the conference to seek new international trade and investment partnerships as an alternative to reliance on the United States. The diplomatic mission also comes amid renewed domestic scrutiny regarding ties between Ottawa and the monarchy.

stories.headline: Quebec Premier Accepts Invitation to Meet Carney After Bilateral Summit Tensions
stories.summary: Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has accepted an invitation to hold bilateral discussions with Prime Minister Mark Carney following disputes during the recent Canada-EU summit in Montreal. The premier had boycotted the Montreal gathering after federal officials refused to grant him formal speaking privileges, and he has requested the upcoming meeting take place in Quebec City. The dialogue aims to address federal-provincial strains prior to the upcoming Francophonie Summit.

stories.headline: Ontario Government Eliminates Minimum Space Rules for Adult Jail Cells
stories.summary: The Ontario government has modified the provincial Building Code to remove regulations requiring at least 4.7 square metres of sleeping area per person in provincial correctional facilities. Civil liberties organizations and prisoner advocacy groups condemned the decision, noting that it was implemented without public consultation and could exacerbate severe overcrowding. Advocates are urging the province to reverse the amendment and establish enforceable living standards for provincial detainees.

articles.title: Ontario government criticized for removing minimum sleeping area rules in jails

stories.headline: Ontario Ministry Investigates Suspected Mass OSAP Application Fraud at Career Colleges
stories.summary: Court records filed by the Ontario government show that more than half of the student financial aid applications at two private career colleges originated from a single computer IP address. The Ministry of Colleges and Universities has placed the institutions under formal scrutiny to determine whether student loans were systematically claimed under false pretences. The probe highlights regulatory vulnerabilities in oversight mechanisms governing provincial financial assistance programs.

articles.title: Thousands of OSAP applications came from a single IP address, ministry alleges

stories.headline: Ontario Proposes Stricter Measures to Shut Down Illicit Cannabis Dispensaries
stories.summary: The Ontario government has unveiled proposed legislative reforms designed to accelerate the closure of illegal brick-and-mortar cannabis shops operating across the province. Licensed retailers welcomed the announcement, noting that illicit sellers have continued to undercut regulated businesses nearly eight years after federal legalization. The proposed rules seek to give municipal and provincial law enforcement enhanced tools to seize illicit products and close down rogue storefronts.

articles.title: Ontario is proposing a crackdown on illegal cannabis stores. Legal retailers say it is long overdue

stories.headline: Police Watchdog Investigates Fare Evasion Arrest That Fractured Teenager's Arm
stories.summary: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has launched an inquiry after a teenager sustained a broken arm during an arrest by Toronto police officers over suspected transit fare evasion. Several teenagers involved stated they had legitimately paid their fares before being aggressively targeted and arrested by officers. The incident has intensified public scrutiny concerning the role of police enforcement and the treatment of youth on the transit system.

articles.title: Police watchdog investigating after boy's arm fractured during arrest over suspected fare evasion: 'Miss, what did I do?'

stories.headline: Incoming Niagara Falls Mayor Requests Public Input on Provincial Casino Plans
stories.summary: The next mayor of Niagara Falls is urging the Ontario government to hold comprehensive public consultations before licensing up to three new casino operators in the city. Premier Doug Ford's administration is pursuing the gaming expansion to boost regional tourism and stimulate commercial investment. Local officials insist that area residents and municipal stakeholders must have an active voice in assessing the local impact of new gaming facilities.

articles.title: Next mayor of Niagara Falls calls for community consultations on Ford’s casino plan

stories.headline: Supreme Court Prepares for Fall Docket Led by Quebec Secularism Law Challenge
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada is scheduled to address several high-profile appeals this November, led by an anticipated ruling concerning Quebec's secularism legislation. The pending decision will clarify the constitutional scope of the notwithstanding clause and delineate the legal protections afforded by the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. The court's judgments this term are expected to have enduring ramifications for human rights protections and provincial legislative authority.

articles.title: Supreme Court of Canada set for busy November with major hearings, pending judgments ahead

stories.headline: Parks Canada Prepares Job Cuts and Reductions to Park Warden Detachments
stories.summary: Parks Canada plans to close at least 13 park warden detachments while eliminating hundreds of staff positions across the country as part of broader operational changes. In Prince Edward Island, more than half of the federal agency's local workforce faces employment uncertainty ahead of the planned reductions. Union representatives and environmental advocates warn that stretching fewer wardens over large areas will threaten wildlife protection and federal park operations.

articles.title: ‘Real people with real lives’: More than half of Parks Canada workers on P.E.I. face uncertainty
